examination\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EWhat is dystonia?\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003EDystonia is a very complex, highly variable neurological movement disorder characterized by involuntary muscle contractions.\u003Cdiv\u003EDystonia results from abnormal functioning of the basal ganglia,a deep part of the brain which helps control coordination of movement.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDystonia may be inherited, acquired, or idiopathic (no known cause). Inherited disorders are transmitted genetically. In acquired forms, dystonia is caused by damage or degeneration of the brain (e.g. after a brain injury or stroke) or exposure to particular drugs. In idiopathic dystonia there is no identifiable cause and no structural damage or degeneration to the brain.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDystonia classification.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChildhood onset – 0 to age 12\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdolescent onset – age 13 to 20\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAdult onset – older than age 20\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFocal dystonia\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFocal dystonia is limited to one area of the body and can affect the neck (cervical dystonia or spasmodic torticollis), eyes (blepharospasm), jaw\/mouth\/lower face (oromandibular dystonia), vocal cords (laryngeal dystonia) or arms\/legs (limb dystonia). Other less common types of focal dystonias can cause unusual stretching, bending or twisting of the trunk (truncal dystonia) or sustained contractions and involuntary, writhing movements of the abdominal wall (abdominal wall dystonia).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESymptoms\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDystonia affects different people in different ways.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBegin in a single area, such as your leg, neck or arm. Focal dystonia that begins after age 21 usually starts in the neck, arm or face. It tends to remain focal or become segmental.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOccur during a specific action, such as writing by hand.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWorsen with stress, fatigue or anxiety.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBecome more noticeable over time.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAreas of the body that can be affected include:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENeck (cervical dystonia). Contractions cause your head to twist and turn to one side, or pull forward or backward, sometimes causing pain.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEjbi45nL83FM8apXn-DM6dQ1-o4MGUzDfvMYtUrLQMdCjbEUrq7AhBw8QEL5UJUDkA4C2cZV6WQyNnEY4gwaQrGqm-p4xMZy5tzeP9xZ4n8boPUkxesVBjAaYVML0k0DCcXoEJwDk1GD9btjV0ScmKt-Ng_snNi3QiWElNlryjCgzNYIzCsPhb6TsGMmG4P\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEjbi45nL83FM8apXn-DM6dQ1-o4MGUzDfvMYtUrLQMdCjbEUrq7AhBw8QEL5UJUDkA4C2cZV6WQyNnEY4gwaQrGqm-p4xMZy5tzeP9xZ4n8boPUkxesVBjAaYVML0k0DCcXoEJwDk1GD9btjV0ScmKt-Ng_snNi3QiWElNlryjCgzNYIzCsPhb6TsGMmG4P\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEyelids. Rapid blinking or spasms cause your eyes to close (blepharospasms) and make it difficult for you to see. Spasms usually aren't painful but might increase when you're in bright light, reading, watching TV, under stress or interacting with people. Your eyes might feel dry, gritty or sensitive to light.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EJaw or tongue (oromandibular dystonia). You might experience slurred speech, drooling, and difficulty chewing or swallowing. Oromandibular dystonia can be painful and often occurs in combination with cervical dystonia or blepharospasm.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EVoice box and vocal cords (laryngeal dystonia). You might have a tight or whispering voice.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHand and forearm. Some types of dystonia occur only while you do a repetitive activity, such as writing (writer's dystonia) or playing a specific musical instrument (musician's dystonia). Symptoms usually don't happen when your arm is at rest.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFocal dystonia more commonly affects people in their 40s and 50s and is frequently referred to as adult-onset dystonia. Women are affected about three times more frequently than men.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDystonia can also be a symptom of another disease or condition, including:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EParkinson's disease\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHuntington's disease\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWilson's disease\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETraumatic brain injury\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBirth injury\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStroke\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EBrain tumor or certain disorders that develop in some people with cancer (paraneoplastic syndromes)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOxygen deprivation or carbon monoxide poisoning\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EInfections, such as tuberculosis or encephalitis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EReactions to certain medications or heavy metal poisoning\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat is drug induced dystonia?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDystonia may occur from administration of dopaminergic\u0026nbsp; agents, lithium ,SSRIs,carbamazepine, and metoclopromaide.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe five characteristics of the drug-induced dystonic reactions are oculogyric crisis, torticollic crisis, buccolingual crisis, opisthotonic crisis, and tortipelvic and gait crisis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETardive dystonia caused by intake of certain drugs. Most commonly, these are antipsychotics or anti nausea drugs which block the dopamine receptors in the brain. Dopamine is found in the basal ganglia and is responsible for normal movement. It has been hypothesized that these drugs can activate an underlying susceptibility in certain individuals.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere are two types of manifestations caused by drugs:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAcute dystonic reactions which typically occur within days to weeks upon starting the offending drug or Tardive dystonia which occurs after a more prolonged (months – years) intake of the drugs.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe potential cause of drug induced dystonia is the development of dopamine receptor hypersensitivity after prolonged blockade of these receptors with the use of antipsychotics or anti emetics. In almost all instances, drug induced dystonias are reversible, resolving after the discontinuation of the offending drug. Tardive dystonia is a rare exception to this rule with a potential for becoming permanent. Tardive syndromes are pretty troublesome since it can be prolonged and very difficult to treat. Treatment involves stopping the offending drug or at least to lower the dose.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWhat is difference between tonic and clinic?\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETonic: Muscles in the body become stiff. Atonic: Muscles in the body relax. Myoclonic: Short jerking in parts of the body. Clonic: Periods of shaking or jerking parts on the body.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca
